items.title: Luxury Sales Plunge in China as Tax Push Hits Wealthy Shoppers
items.summary: Bloomberg reports sales at China's 25 biggest luxury labels fell more than 10% in July 2026, worse than June, as Beijing's campaign to tax offshore wealth curbs spending by the richest consumers. Louis Vuitton, Dior, and Kering's Gucci, Bottega Veneta and Balenciaga all recorded double-digit declines; Hermes swung from gains to losses. Framed as the biggest shake-up of China's cross-border financial system in a decade.

items.title: Europe's Luxury Giants Discern Green Shoots in Key China Market
items.summary: Follow-up Bloomberg piece noting Kering CEO Luca de Meo called China a 'top strategic priority' and consensus expects Kering/Gucci to return to growth in the China-inclusive region by Q4 2026, even as July's double-digit sector-wide sales drop persists; LVMH and Burberry cited tentative stabilization signs (Sephora, Greater China retail +9%) as a counterpoint to the tax-driven slump.

items.title: Kering Stock Reacts to China Luxury Slowdown as Investors Weigh Gucci Recovery
items.summary: Market wire reports Kering shares fell roughly 3.6% in the August 24 session after fresh reporting on weak Chinese luxury demand renewed scrutiny of Gucci's turnaround, with shares trading in the mid-EUR250 range and down double digits year-to-date; described as a recalibration of near-term earnings expectations rather than a fundamental brand-strength shift.

items.title: Demna's Runway Debut at Gucci Was 'More Good Than Bad,' Says Bernstein
items.summary: WWD relays Bernstein luxury analyst Luca Solca's assessment that Demna's first Gucci runway show drew a mixed but net-positive reaction, cited alongside continued analyst caution that gradual China demand improvement remains below expectations -- a balancing data point between creative reception and the harder commercial China narrative dominating the week's coverage.

items.title: 매출 성장, 신규 매장 개설… 외자 기업 실적 속 중국 기회
items.summary: Chinese state-media Korean-language business roundup on foreign firms' China performance and new-store openings, cited by regional analysts as illustrating the split narrative in China: some multinational retailers still expanding store footprints even as headline luxury-sector sales (including Gucci) contract on the tax-driven demand pullback.

items.title: グッチが新作バッグ「ジャッキー フラップ」発売
items.summary: Japanese trade outlet fashionsnap reports Gucci's launch of the new 'Jackie Flap' bag from the Primavera collection, derived from the archival Gucci Jackie silhouette with piston-closure hardware; available in canvas (473,000 yen) and leather (539,000 yen) versions, convertible between shoulder and crossbody wear -- product-launch signal balancing the heavier China macro coverage in this pool.
